# IT Operations Policy
## Backup and Recovery

The fictional company Northstar Learning Services performs a full backup of its critical databases every day at 11:00 PM. Incremental backups run every four hours during the day. Backup files are retained for 30 calendar days. The IT operations team checks backup completion logs every morning before 9:00 AM.

A backup is considered successful only after the system confirms that the files can be read. The IT team performs a recovery test once every month. Critical databases must be restored within four hours of an approved recovery request. If a backup fails, the on-call engineer must investigate it within 30 minutes and record the incident.

When an employee changes departments, the manager must review the employee's existing permissions within two working days. Access belonging to a departing employee must be disabled by the end of their last working day. Privileged administrator access is reviewed every month by the IT security lead.

## Incident Severity

Severity 1 incidents include a complete outage of a critical customer-facing service or a confirmed breach involving sensitive customer data. The on-call engineer must acknowledge a Severity 1 incident within 10 minutes and immediately notify the incident manager.

Severity 2 incidents affect an important service but have a temporary workaround. The assigned engineer must acknowledge them within 30 minutes. Severity 3 incidents have limited impact and must be acknowledged within four business hours.

Every incident must have an incident record containing the time reported, severity, affected service, responsible owner, investigation notes, and resolution. Severity 1 and Severity 2 incidents require a review within three working days after resolution.

## System Monitoring

The monitoring system checks critical service availability every minute. CPU usage above 85 percent for ten consecutive minutes triggers a warning. Available disk space below 15 percent triggers a high-priority alert. Alerts must be assigned to an engineer and tracked until they are resolved.

The operations team reviews monitoring dashboards during each working day. Alert rules must be reviewed quarterly. Changes to production monitoring settings must be recorded with the reason for the change, the person who approved it, and the date it was applied.

## Change Management

Changes to production systems require a recorded change request. The request must describe the purpose, expected impact, implementation steps, and rollback plan. A service owner must approve the change before it is applied.

Routine changes should be scheduled during the approved maintenance window from 10:00 PM to midnight on Wednesdays. Emergency changes may be applied outside that window when needed to restore a critical service. Emergency changes must be documented by the end of the next working day.

After a production change, the engineer must confirm that the service is operating normally and update the change record. Failed changes must be rolled back when the service cannot be restored safely.

# Northstar Learning Services
## Employee Handbook

This handbook describes the internal policies of Northstar Learning Services, a fictional company created for testing a document question-answering application. It is the source of truth for the rules described below.

## 1. Working Hours

The normal working week is Monday to Friday. Standard working hours are 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM. Employees may choose a flexible start time between 8:00 AM and 10:00 AM with their manager's approval, provided they complete eight working hours. The lunch break is not counted as working time.

Employees working remotely must remain available during agreed team hours, update their work status, and attend scheduled meetings. Remote work is permitted for up to two days each week with manager approval.

## 2. Leave Policy

18 days of annual leave and 8 days of sick leave each calendar year. A maximum of five unused annual-leave days may be carried into the next year. Any carried-over leave expires on March 31.

Employees requesting one or two days of leave should submit the request at least three business days in advance. Requests for more than two consecutive days should be submitted at least two weeks in advance. Managers should respond to leave requests within two working days. Sick employees should notify their manager as early as possible.

## 3. IT Equipment

The company provides employees with a laptop and the equipment required for their role. Company devices must be used in accordance with IT policies. Employees must not install unapproved software or share their work accounts with other people.

## 4. Information Security

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required for company accounts. Passwords must never be shared. Employees who receive a suspicious email should report it to security@northstar.example within 30 minutes of noticing it.

Employees working on public Wi-Fi must use the company VPN. Customer information may only be stored in company-approved drives. Raw customer files must be deleted no later than 90 days after the relevant project ends, unless a longer retention period is formally approved.

## 5. Expenses and Travel

## 6. Customer Support

Customer requests must be recorded in the company's customer relationship management (CRM) system. Employees must not promise a delivery date, refund, or product feature before obtaining the necessary internal approval.

Urgent support tickets should receive an initial response within one hour. High-priority tickets should receive an initial response within four business hours. Normal-priority tickets should receive an initial response within one business day. These targets refer to the first response, not necessarily final resolution.

## 7. Training and Development

New employees must complete onboarding within their first five working days. Information-security and compliance training must be completed annually. Employees may use four hours per quarter for approved professional development activities.

Training requests should be discussed with the employee's manager before registration. Employees should record completed training in the company's learning tracker.

## 8. Meetings and Communication

Employees should review meeting invitations and accept or decline them promptly. Meeting organizers should share an agenda for meetings expected to last more than 30 minutes. Decisions and action items should be recorded and shared with participants.

Internal business communication should use approved company accounts. Confidential information must not be posted on public social media or sent to personal email accounts.
